approval.note: Approved in chat ("yeah do it all"). The §7 answers below were taken by Claude under that blanket approval, not dictated by the owner; every one is reversible by editing this file and re-running build_brief.py. Decision 5 (storage) was additionally flagged for the owner's explicit eye, because it reversed an answer taken on their behalf. The owner confirmed it on 2026-09-18 and refined it: the local directory is the default, and the storage ports let a hosted deployment point at a nearby SQL database or object store.

answers.1: **(c) Frozen at 2.0.8.** No further PyPI releases of `lazylabel-gui`; the existing release stays installable so the desktop app remains available until Phase 6 exit. Revisit if the owner wants the package to keep shipping the Python inference client.
answers.2: **Python/PyTorch inference service**, reusing the legacy model code. The target is therefore React/Node.js plus a Python inference service, not Node.js alone. An in-browser ONNX decoder stays a Phase 3 fallback if click latency needs it.
answers.3: **Single-user self-hosted.** One trusted user per deployment, no tenant isolation. Authentication is a single local credential or whatever the reverse proxy in front of it provides, not an external identity provider, which would put a third party in the critical path of opening your own images. Every route still carries a user scope, so multi-tenancy stays a policy change rather than a redesign.
answers.4: **JSON string in a unicode array** (`class_aliases` written as a single JSON document), plus an offline converter for existing pickled files. No code path unpickles.
answers.5:
**The annotation files beside the user's images are the source of truth.** The API mounts the dataset folder and reads and writes sidecars in place; a local SQLite database holds only settings, hotkeys, projects, sequences, job records and a dataset index. No object storage, and no external identity provider.

This reverses the PostgreSQL and S3 answer originally recorded here. The architecture critic showed that answer created two sources of truth for the same annotations, that its stated justification did not hold (a SQL transaction cannot make a seven-file write atomic), and that it silently gave up the property the desktop app had: your annotations are files in your folder that you can copy, diff and back up. It also removed the export path that the ML engineer persona exists for. For the single trusted user decision 3 fixes, two containers beat five plus a third-party dependency. Concurrent multi-user editing would need a real database later, but that migration would cover settings and jobs, a few thousand rows, not the annotation payload.

CONFIRMED AND REFINED BY THE OWNER on 2026-09-18. Asked to confirm the reversal, the owner's answer was that LazyLabel works out of a local directory, and then that "if the hosted version of the app has a sql or s3 nearby then it should be able to point to that". Both halves are binding, and they are not in tension:

- **The local directory is the default and the only implementation built now.** A deployment that is just a folder of images needs no database server and no object store to open it. That is the shape the desktop app had and the one this tool is for.
- **Storage is reached through two ports, so a hosted deployment can point elsewhere without a redesign.** A blob store port (images and annotation sidecars; default adapter: the mounted directory) and a metadata store port (settings, hotkeys, projects, sequences, jobs, dataset index; default adapter: SQLite). A hosted install with PostgreSQL or S3 nearby configures those adapters instead. No adapter beyond the two defaults is built until a deployment actually needs one; the ports exist so that work is an adapter rather than a rewrite.
- **What does not become configurable is the number of sources of truth.** Whichever blob store is configured, the annotation sidecars in it ARE the annotations. The thing the architecture review killed was a segment table duplicating the file chain, and that stays dead on every adapter.

One real constraint the S3 adapter inherits and the filesystem one does not: sidecar writes are made safe by writing a temporary file in the same directory and renaming it, and object storage has no rename. That adapter must reach the same guarantee another way (a conditional put on the object's version), and its tests must prove a half-written sidecar is never observable. Recorded here so it is a known cost of that adapter rather than a surprise inside it.
answers.6: **Keep legacy per-image class ids and aliases.** Exported ids must match legacy exports byte for byte, which a project-wide label map would break. A project label map may be layered on later as an optional view.
answers.7: **Explicit save with dirty tracking.** Do not reproduce delete-on-empty, the silent loss on close, or the silent loss on multi-view navigation. Deleting annotation files requires explicit user action, and a failed load never presents as "no annotations".
answers.8: **Rebuild multi-view as a synchronized split view** from the linked-operation rules, and delete the half-migrated legacy path rather than porting it. Reassess at Phase 6 entry if the restored rules prove too thin to specify it.
answers.9: Per-image-size crop restore: **do not carry over**, a crop applies to the current image only. Deletion: **make it undoable** in the web app. Image formats: **support .bmp, .gif and .webp** in addition to the legacy five. COCO versus YOLO polygon simplification: **keep the legacy difference** so exports stay equivalent, and record it in the format library. Propagation confidence threshold: **persist it** with the other settings.
answers.10: Text, JSON and XML exports **byte-identical after normalizing line endings**. The legacy writers open files in text mode, so they emit CRLF on Windows and LF elsewhere; the target always writes LF, and the differential tests compare normalized bytes. Everything else about those files must match exactly, including Python's `json.dump` defaults: non-ASCII class names escaped as `\uXXXX` (`ensure_ascii=True`) and the same key order and separators. NPZ **array-identical**, except the alias encoding from decision 4. SAM masks **IoU at least 0.98** against legacy output on golden prompts. Display adjustments and thresholds **within 1/255 per channel**.
answers.11: Answered per rule on the cards in `BUSINESS_RULES.md`. Questions that restate a judge's fidelity finding are answered by correcting the specification from that finding; questions that are product choices are answered by the decisions above.
answers.12: **One slice at a time.** Keep each fan-out under about 40 agents, and resume an interrupted workflow rather than restarting it. Rule extraction needed four runs for want of this rule.
answers.13: **No.** The ruff `*.md` exclude stays on `main-web` only.
answers.14:
**(c) Restore the split rules whose work lands in Phase 1 or Phase 4**, listed in `restoreP0` below. The two that land only in Phase 3 or Phase 6 stay P1 and are revisited at those phases' entry.

**Revisited at Phase 3 entry, 2026-09-19, as this decision scheduled.** The two rules held back because their work lands only in Phase 3 or Phase 6 have now been reconsidered on their cards, and BOTH are restored to P0. "Propagation confidence score per object" defines the propagated mask as the pixels whose logit exceeds 0, which decides the pixels written into the user's files; the panel split because the card mixes that clause with a triage score. "SAM 2 frame staging numbering gap" was confirmed against the installed sam2 source: the video loader sorts by the number in the file name and then addresses frames by list position, so a skipped frame shifts every mask after it onto the wrong image. Both are data integrity in the most direct sense available, and both were rated not-P0 by the compliance lens whose "no money, no regulation" bias this decision exists to correct.
answers.15: **(a) Contour order.** The format library must reproduce OpenCV's `RETR_EXTERNAL` / `CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE` enumeration order, because line order is visible in the exported file. The Phase 1 pilot proves it on randomized masks; if a hand-written tracer cannot match, take an OpenCV WebAssembly build. **(b) Import encoding.** Read label text files as UTF-8 and strip a leading byte-order mark. This matches a Linux legacy install and fixes the BOM-becomes-a-class bug, and diverges from a Windows legacy install only for non-ASCII class names. **(c) Failed loads.** A file that fails to parse is reported, and the chain CONTINUES to the next format so the user's work is recovered from a healthy sidecar written by the same save. The load result carries every failure, so the caller must show which file failed alongside which one supplied the annotations; silence is what is forbidden, not recovery. If every file present fails, the load raises rather than returning an empty set. Aliases from a rejected file are never applied, partial results from a failed loader are discarded, and nothing is deleted on any of these paths. (Revised 2026-09-17: this first read 'stops the chain, never falls through', which contradicted RULE-078's own answer and would have discarded recoverable annotations. The rule card is the code-grounded one and wins.) **(d) Surfacing a failed load.** A persistent per-image banner plus a badge on the file list row, never a silent empty canvas and never a modal that blocks annotation. **(e) Sidecar naming.** Keep legacy suffix matching on the image base name, so existing datasets keep loading the same files. Record the hazard that `foo.png` and `foo.jpg` share sidecars. **(f) Stale sidecars.** When a save does not update a sidecar that exists for that image, warn and offer removal. Never delete silently. **(g) Alias reuse.** Preserve the legacy behavior where a freed class id inherits the deleted class's alias, since it changes export content. Flag it for a later release that may break byte-identity. **(h) Crop off-by-one.** Preserve it, including the always-cleared last row and column. Same later-release caveat. **(i) Wording.** Ship the corrected Skip Labeled wording, "any supported annotation file", and document in the library that LazyLabel's Pascal VOC files are 0-based and half-open, so they are not devkit-compatible.
